content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <=9999. Need to find templates. We can search for sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Also amide formation (acid chloride + amine). The target has a sulfonamide linking a tolyl sulfonyl group to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline.

Structure: p-methyl phenyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring (para to methyl) which is attached to sulfonamide linking to another phenyl ring (the second phenyl is para-substituted with a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually the amide attaches to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So the amide carbonyl attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). The amide is conjugated with a trans double bond.

Thus retrosynthesis: disconnection 1: sulfonamide bond between tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) and an aniline (the phenyl ring bearing the unsaturated amide). So we can get p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (commercial) and the amine component: the phenyl ring with the unsaturated amide and an NH2 (aniline). That amine is the second phenyl with amide side chain.

Second disconnection: amide bond between aniline (aniline with para NH2) and acryloyl chloride (or acryloyl derivative). Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the amide formed from acryloyl chloride (CH2=CH-COCl) reacting with aniline (para-aminophenyl). That yields trans? Might need to control geometry but okay.

Thus route: Step 1: sulfonamide formation: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride + (para-aminophenyl)acrylamide (the amide product). Step 2: amide formation: acryloyl chloride + p-phenylenediamine? Wait the amine component is aniline with para NH2 (i.e., 4-aminophenyl). The product after amide formation is N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide (i.e., 4-aminophenyl acrylamide). That still has an NH2 para to the amide. So we need p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene) as starting material, then acylate one amine with acryloyl chloride, leaving the other amine free for sulfonamide later. So step 2: selective monoacylation of p-phenylenediamine with acryloyl chloride (maybe using protecting group). But we can also start from 4-aminophenylamine (p-phenylenediamine) and protect one amine (e.g., Boc) then acylate, then deprotect, then sulfonylate. That adds steps.

But we have max 3 steps. Could we use 4-aminobenzaldehyde? Not.

Alternative: Use 4-aminophenyl is commercially available (p-phenylenediamine). Use sulfonyl chloride first to form sulfonamide on one amine, then acylate the other amine with acryloyl chloride. That yields final product with both sulfonamide and amide. Order can be swapped.

Thus step 1: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride + p-phenylenediamine -> sulfonamide (mono-sulfonylated). Need selectivity; but maybe commercially available p-tolylsulfonyl chloride reacts preferentially with one amine; could be mixture but assume.

Step 2: acryloyl chloride reacts with remaining amine to give amide.

Thus only 2 steps. Leaves: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride, p-phenylenodiamine, acryloyl chloride. All commercially available and cheap.

We need to verify buyability. Use is_buyable for each.
